chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who fabricated (a slander) upon a group of people. He said: If they come with it together, he is whipped with one penalty (Hadd); and if they come with it separately, he is whipped for each man, one penalty (Hadd).
ai.seo_question: How is the penalty for slander determined when a man accuses a group of people?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the procedural application of the hadd penalty for qadhf (slander) when targeting a collective group, distinguishing between joint and individual litigation. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that the number of penalties corresponds to the number of distinct legal claims presented, ensuring justice in both consolidated and fragmented accusations. This ruling underscores the importance of procedural clarity in establishing the fixed punishment for slander.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad Bin Humran,

(The narrator) says, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a man who fabricated upon a group of people. So heasws said: ‘If they come with it altogether, he would be whipped one Penalty (Hadd), and if they come with it seperately, he would be whipped for each man, one Penalty (Hadd)’.
